images.caption: Figure 2:Games created by VibeGame from prompts across diverse 2D game genres.

Figure 3:System overview of VibeGame.(a) The Adversarial Agent Team turns a user request into an accepted game through intention alignment, parallel development, and adversarial correction. (b) The AI-native game engine exposes a structured project representation and frame-synchronous runtime control for implementation and play-testing. (c) Training-free self-evolution extracts skeletons, modules, and collaboration contracts from accepted projects and returns them to future development as project priors.
Figure 5:Qualitative comparison between VibeGame, Codex (PA2G), and Codex (P2G), all using GPT-6.1-Sol.Left: Sports Skateboard Park. Right: Sports Boxing Gym. Red boxes mark the defects.

Figure 6:Judge error case 1: Kimi Code + GPT-5.6-Luna (P2G) on Racing Drift Circuit. The judged track-select frame: its twelve thumbnails reuse four layouts, one per biome (e.g., the three Canyon tracks share one layout).
Figure 7:Judge error case 2: OpenGame + GPT-5.6-Luna on Cardgame Autobattler. The board has a front and a back row (BACK 2–4) and no bench; the board heading and row labels are covered by cards.

Figure 8:Judge error case 3: Kimi Code + GPT-5.6-Luna (P2G) on Idle Factory Planet. Three consecutive judged frames, cropped to one production chain and shown at the source recording’s 1280×\times720 resolution (the judges received them downscaled to 854×\times480): conveyors connect the four machines and the resource particles move along them.

Figure 9:Game creation demonstrations.Top: Pixel Sekiro, a pixel-art boss fight created from a text prompt. Bottom: Hollow Knight boss slice, a side-scrolling boss fight created from a gameplay prompt and a concept image.

Figure 10:Game edit demonstrations.Top: intellectual property (IP) transfer, replacing the visual theme while preserving gameplay logic. Middle: genre transfer, converting a turn-based card game into a real-time boss fight while preserving its visual identity. Bottom: rule transfer, swapping the player and boss roles while preserving their abilities and animations.
